summary: Allocated free-tier bucket shadowing during multi-region cutover causing reserved-credit hold on invoice
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NimbleAssist noticed a reserved credit line (~$1,200) appearing on their March invoice after our multi-region cutover on 2026-03-11. The reserved credit references free-tier buffer allocation and shows as a provisional hold (Line 3B: 'reserved_free_buffer_us-east').

Impact:
- Invoice shows a reserved credit reducing available balance; customer cannot auto-pay until hold resolved.
- Customer reports unexpected "missing" free-tier consumption (tokens appear unconsumed in dashboard), and alerts triggered for sudden reduction in available credits.
- Business impact: NimbleAssist (enterprise) blocked on monthly billing reconciliation for procurement.

Environment:
- Production tenant for NimbleAssist, primarily routed through us-east after cutover. Some async postbacks landed in eu-west during flow.

Steps to reproduce / observed behavior:
1) Cutover process applied new region tags and billing_tag rewrite for multi-tenant reconciler at 2026-03-11T02:10Z.
2) Customer ran regular batch evaluation and streaming traffic between 2026-03-11T04:00Z and 2026-03-11T08:30Z.
3) Billing reconciler created provisional hold lines referencing reserved_free_buffer_us-east and did not consume tokens; aggregator shows two different tag values for the same API key.
4) Invoice generation job picked up provisional holds on 2026-03-12T00:45Z.

Expected behavior:
- Free-tier buffer allocation should be applied and consumed immediately on usage or released if unused; no provisional reserved credit should be left on finalized invoice.

Observed behavior:
- Reserved credit persisted and blocked autopay; customer-facing dashboard shows token usage but billing postbacks show offset to a separate pseudo-org tag.

Logs / evidence attached:
- Billing reconciler logs snippet: reconciler.job: 'tag_rewrite: applied override to api_key *******abcd -> billing_tag: neo-us-east-archive' (attachment: reconciler_logs_20260311.txt)
- Invoice snapshot: invoice_2026-03-12_nimbleassist.pdf (line showing reserved_free_buffer_us-east)
comments: 2026-03-12 Priya Shah (Support): Opened with customer after procurement escalation. Provided provisional explanation and requested permission to run admin credit release. Linked to #billing in Slack.

2026-03-12 Ethan Morales (Billing): Investigating reconciler run and postback ordering. Early hypothesis: tag rewrite duplicated buffer allocation in postback namespace; requested reconciler logs and postback id list.

2026-03-13 Lina Berg (SRE): Confirmed reconciler PR 4321 ran during maintenance window and altered tag normalization for a subset of customers; found partial replay of postbacks from eu-west queue that used old tag. Evidence: postback IDs 98765, 98766 show inconsistent tags.

2026-03-13 Priya Shah (Support): Customer confirmed they did not manually apply any promotions. Provided consent for admin credit release and asked for ETA to resolve invoice hold (urgent for autopay).

2026-03-14 Ethan Morales (Billing): Temporary workaround executed: released reserved_free_buffer_us-east hold via billing-admin (audit id AUD-20260314-77). Issued credit memo CM-5698 for $1,200 and set invoice to 'adjusted'. Informing customer and finance.
investigation_notes: Reconciler tag rewrite produced a shadowed billing namespace: some postbacks kept old tenant_tag while reconciler created a new reserved_bucket entry under new tag. This left tokens visible in usage dashboard but unclaimed by billing namespace.
Out-of-order postback replay from eu-west queue (delayed by ~18 minutes) meant reconciler ran twice for same logical usage with different tags: one consumption record and one reservation record.
Rate-limiting on postback consumer caused backpressure and duplicate reconciliation attempts; consumer backoff retries had idempotency key mismatch for patched tag formatting change.

Affected customers appear to be those with hybrid-hosted + private routing that touched both regions during the cutover window; estimated impacted invoices ~10-12 customers with combined provisional holds ~$8k.
Related code change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reconciler/pull/4321 altered billing_tag normalization to include region suffix which interacted badly with legacy postbacks.
resolution_notes: Workaround: billing-admin released reserved holds for NimbleAssist and issued credit memo CM-5698. We set invoice to adjusted and enabled autopay. Long-term fix: rollback tag normalization change in reconciler (PR 4321) and deploy idempotency key safeguard for postback consumer. Follow-ups: INT ticket to run a scan and release remaining orphaned reserved_free_buffer_* holds for impacted customers; add additional helm readiness gating for reconciler during region cutovers.
next_steps: INT- cleanup run: run audit script to find reserved_free_buffer_* holds created between 2026-03-11T01:50Z and 2026-03-11T03:30Z and auto-release or queue for manual review (owner: Ethan Morales)
Revert PR 4321 or patch: add idempotency on tag normalization and add integration test to cover cross-region postback ordering (owner: Lina Berg)
Communicate to affected customers: send tailored update emails and sticky credits where appropriate (owner: CS team)
Add postmortem to Confluence and link to status page event if more than 5 customers impacted (owner: Ops)
public_notes_for_customer: We discovered that a recent reconciler change during the region cutover caused a provisional reserved credit line to be created for your account. We released the hold and issued a credit memo so autopay can proceed. Our engineering team will follow up with a permanent fix and will notify you when a postmortem is available.
customer_response_summary: 2026-03-14 NimbleAssist finance confirmed invoice updated and autopay successful; requested written confirmation and root cause within 48 hours.
